p2c1.opener_idea: GRAND band (12rem) + extended caption. Plate: institute mass on dead hills, single amber window, river as converging line. Kicker: PART II · EITHER-OR (Space Mono, amber). Head: THE MAN WHO BELONGED ON EARTH (Barlow Condensed 600). Data line: CHAPTER I · 19954 WORDS. Amber rule, left-weighted. Caption: SIG II-01 · 19954 WORDS. First body line visible without scroll at 1440x1000.
p2c1.palette_role: Order Amber (#E8A33D) carries the single office-window lamp only; hills in Railsteel (#8B98A5) flat slabs on Nightballast (#0E1216); slot well Tunnelblack (#07090C). No green/red anywhere — caution is the whole statement.
p2c1.proposed_motif: The State Science Institute as a dark slab mass on dead-gray hills above a black river at night, ONE amber window burning (Stadler's office); the river drawn as a single converging line toward the lit window. Dead hills as flat Railsteel slabs; no glow on the window — flat disc + hard 2px halo ring per the signal medium.
p2c1.rationale: Opens on Dr. Stadler pacing his Institute office above the dead-gray hills and leaden river (:0), dreading Ferris's book Why Do You Think You Think? (:5-13). Middle: Project X / Xylophone secrecy (:50-57), the 10,000-ton Rearden Metal order for Project X (:224-226) which Rearden refuses (:303). Closes with Rearden and Dagny grasping the looters' fear (:443-449). Title referent verified: Rearden is 'a man who belonged on earth' (:357). The plate stages the chapter's true subject — institutional science under orders, one mind's lamp still lit — rather than illustrating the romance plot.

read_coverage.middle_note: Sampled Institute/Project X order/refusal/party scenes (:18-421); full middle not read cover-to-cover.

p2c7.opener_idea: GRAND band (12rem) + extended caption. Plate: portal mouth, smoke slab, swallowed wedge. Kicker: PART II · EITHER-OR. Head: THE MORATORIUM ON BRAINS. Data line: CHAPTER VII · 20134 WORDS. Amber rule, left-weighted. Caption: SIG II-07 · 20134 WORDS. Heaviest subject in the part; the plate is smoke, not spectacle — no bodies, no wreckage detail.
p2c7.palette_role: Amber carries the portal lamp ONLY — one lamp over the mouth. Smoke as a flat Railsteel slab (never a blur, never a gradient); the Comet's headlight wedge Headlight but visibly swallowed mid-plate. Explicitly NO red intruder: the stopped-world red belongs to Part III, and Wyatt's Torch already owns flame in this book. Discipline is the horror.
p2c7.proposed_motif: The tunnel mouth at night (the Winston portals under the Rockies): black arch, one amber lamp above it, and a flat slab of smoke pouring out to fill two-thirds of the plate — inside the smoke, the Comet's headlight wedge half-swallowed (verified mechanics: coal-burner forced through, :270-327; Chalmers: 'if you don't start that train...' :327). 30 Comet hits, 22 tunnel hits — the densest disaster vocabulary in the book. The plate shows the moment after: smoke where a train went in.
p2c7.rationale: Opens double: Eddie in the underground cafeteria (:0), then Rearden's night walk from the mills (:1-11) to his starlit-road meeting with Ragnar Danneskjold (:12-180; 'a disembodied train... going past them in the night' :150). Middle: the dispatchers' fight over the Comet (:256-292), Chalmers forcing the tunnel run (:314-327), the buck-passing chain (:340-430). Closes with the passenger roster — each berth a condemned idea (:440-454) — ending on Wyatt's Torch as the last thing seen (:454). Title = the Directive's freeze on minds. The plate withholds the roster and the road meeting both: the tunnel mouth is the image the whole novel remembers.

read_coverage.middle_note: Sampled Danneskjold meeting, dispatch crisis, tunnel forcing (:14-430); full middle not read cover-to-cover.

coverage_gaps: Openings read 14 paras each (requirement: 10+); closings read 8 paras each (requirement: 5+); middles scene-sampled with verified para cites, NOT read cover-to-cover for any chapter. No full-text read of the money speech (p2c2:324-339), the trial address (p2c4), the Directive text (p2c6), or the Starnesville story (p2c10) — motifs keyed to verified passages only. No invented events: every scene cited above was observed in the chapter JSON; 'Taggart Tunnel' and 'ray-shield' are supervisor shorthand, not text terms, and the file avoids asserting them as text.

grammar.amber_logic: Part II = amber/caution: orders contradict orders; the Line runs on fear. Every plate carries exactly one amber function (window, lamp row, lamp, joint-lamp, board lamp + numerals, portal lamp, cabin window, hanging lamp, engraved dollar) — never decoration.
grammar.intruder_policy: NO intruders in Part II. p2c7's catastrophe stays amber (smoke, not flame; red belongs to Part III). p2c10's dollar is flat amber line-work, not gold (A2). The identity's documented intruders (p1c10, p3c1, p3c10) are untouched.
grammar.medium: Flat night-lithograph SVG per identity.json: solid ink slabs, 2-3 flat hues per plate + lamp color, converging-line perspective, beams as flat wedges, lamps as flat discs with hard 2px halo rings. NEVER glow, NEVER gradients, NEVER gold. Linework >= 2px at final size.
grammar.no_index_correlation: Plate weights and motifs are authored per chapter from para counts + verified scenes (identity.json scale determination), never computed from chapter index. No odd/even alternation. Grand: p2c1, p2c2, p2c3, p2c4, p2c7, p2c10. Standard: p2c5, p2c6. Compact: p2c8, p2c9.

references_studied: Identity draft reference set (directions.md S0, inherited): Cassandre Etoile du Nord railway-poster idiom (V&A O74368 catalogue description — converging rails head-on, one huge idea per plate); Salter 1957 Atlas jacket (LBI Griffinger 5525297 record — tunnel-mouth + converging rails + signal-disc primitives); Ferriss massing-before-detail; 1930s Fortune industrial-lush covers; Rodchenko/Lissitzky 2-3 flat hues + type-as-structure; Fountainhead APPROVED submission shape (F1-F10).

Railway signal idioms (this designer, catalogue-record grounding, no pixels claimed): Smithsonian Handlan hand-signal kerosene lantern 1930s-40s (nmah_841602) — the hand-lamp as the signal medium's human scale; railsigns.uk semaphore histories + Wikipedia railway semaphore signal — blade-by-day / color-by-night aspect logic behind the caution grammar.

Cassandre night-poster idiom (this designer, catalogue records): V&A Voyages la Nuit en Wagons-Lits (O1029907), V&A Normandie (O1405126); MoMA Watch the Fords Go By 1937 (7296), MoMA New York via Le Havre 1935 (5138) — flat night lithography, geometric transport romanticism. Lesson applied: plates as flat slabs + converging lines, never rendered scenes.

Negative references honored: no banknote-guilloche borders (Direction B rejected — survives only as the p2c10 dollar line-work detail inside the signal grammar); no departure-board grids (Direction C rejected); no gold glow, no cream/terracotta, no SaaS cards, no eyebrow chrome (frontend-design default cluster).

scale_legend.law: First body line visible without scroll at 1440x1000 for standard openers; grand/compact scale the BAND, never the text zone.
